pull.title: KAFKA-20669: Fix Consumer propagates stale TopicAuthorizationException/InvalidTopicException after subscription change
pull.body:
Problem-maybeFailOnMetadataError and
OffsetsRequestManager.maybeCompleteWithPreviousException   propagate
stored metadata errors without checking if they still apply to the
consumer's current topics.       After assign() or subscribe()
switchestopics,   the next AsyncPollEvent  can inherit a stale
TopicAuthorizationException or InvalidTopicException.      This blocked
the consumer group protocol rows of
testNoDescribeProduceOrConsumeWithoutTopicDescribeAcl.

  Fix-ConsumerUtils.isErrorProvablyUnrelated — returns true iff the
error's topics are disjoint from the current set.     Handles
TopicAuthorizationException / InvalidTopicException,   unwraps
CompletionException.  ApplicationEventProcessor.currentlyRelevantTopics
— unions  subscription() and assignedPartitions() so the check covers
both paths.  Both call sites consult the helper before dispatching.

  Ran PlaintextEndToEndAuthorizationTest locally 50 times all passed.
  ```shell
  N=50; I=0; while [ $I -lt $N ] && ./gradlew core:test --tests
"kafka.api.*EndToEndAuthorization*.testNoDescribeProduceOrConsumeWithoutTopicDescribeAcl*"
  --rerun --fail-fast; do (( I=$I+1 )); echo "Completed run: $I"; sleep
1; done
  ```

Reviewers: Lianet Magrans <lmagrans@confluent.io>, Chia-Ping Tsai
 <chia7712@gmail.com>

reviews.body: Hi, good catch! High level comment on the approach. This is filtering out metadata errors for topics that are not in the subscription, but that may affect APIs like offsetsForTimes/beginning/endOffsets I imagine (all that's behind the ListOffsets event). Those add topics to metadata temporarily ("transientTopics"), unrelated to the subscribed/assigned ones, and we need to propagate errors for them too, aren't we loosing them?
Thanks @kuoche1712003 ! Some other thoughts, hope it helps, tricky

review_comments.body: May be better to use a constant for `200`, instead of hardcoding.

Good point — I looked into this. In this specific path the chain stays on plain CompletableFuture (never 
crosses KafkaFutureImpl), and the JDK's CompletableFuture.encodeThrowable reuses an existing 
CompletionException rather than re-wrapping, so nesting shouldn't occur here. ExecutionException only 
surfaces via Future.get(), while we capture the error in a whenComplete callback.

Existing single-layer unwraps in Errors.maybeUnwrapException:541 and ApplicationEventProcessor:815 follow the same reasoning, so I kept this consistent — but I'm happy to switch to a multi-layer loop if you'd prefer the extra safety margin. Let me know which you'd like.
Done, thanks!

review_comments.body: Done, thanks!
I don't have a strong opinion about unwrapping, but will leave it to 2nd reviewer.
Should we log it before those "unrelated" errors disappear
Done, thanks!

would this make more sense in the SubscriptionState class?

Seems a kind of subscribedOrAssignedTopics() to me (exclusive, we can never have both at the same time)
I wonder if we were intentionally using the for loop and avoiding the streams api because we're in the hot path here? (this is called on each iteration of the background thread loop)
Good point, I'll move it to SubscriptionState.
Thanks for the heads up! I'll keep the for loop.

uhm this piece of logic seems to overlap with bits that already exist in metadata and subscription state, wonder if we should review them all to avoid ending up with different ways to identify the same (if a topic's metadata is relevant)

E.g, `metadataTopics` (doesn't it already tell us the same as the new "subscribedOrAssignedTopics"?), also `retainTopic` (this is what we already use to know if the client keeps the metadata entry from response or drops it, also `needsMetadata`

Ideally I would aim for a hook here on the metadata component, that just puts together all the hooks we already have to determine if a topic is still "relevant" (so we can be sure it's ok to throw the exception".  Maybe a combination of isTransient || needsMetadata || [regex, this seems a missing bit to consider in the PR?]...Still not 100% sure this is all but for sure it's part of it

I'm still nervous about this :) 

E.g., I don't see we consider regex. Client-side old regex, metadata for all topics is resolved on the client to compute it, would we drop auth errors here? Similar thought for the new R2j regex
Agree, makes sense to consolidate. Let me go through the existing checks and the regex case and I’ll follow up.
